newsitem.title: CHINA: PRESS DIGEST - Chinese newspapers - Jan 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Chinese newspapers - Jan 3.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Chinese political and business stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Beijing. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy. Telephone: (8610) 6532-1921. Fax: (8610) 6532-4978.
A front page commentary says further opening of the economy, especially in foreign trade and the use of foreign funds, is necessary to meet new challenges and come in line with the world economy.
The State Council, or cabinet, issues a circular urging the central and local governments to take measures to stabilise prices during the upcoming Spring Festival, or Chinese New Year.
The State Planning Commission and the Ministry of Finance abolish 48 fees levied on residential housing construction as part of a drive to boost commercial housing development.
China's cotton demand is seen at five million tonnes in 1997 and imports are expected to be at a fairly high level.
The Ministry of Geology and Mineral Resources will this year end state funding to most of its exploration and mining units, forcing them into the market to stand on their own feet.
Deutsche Telecom and Chinese telecommunications authorities are moving ahead with a $250 million cooperation project that could become a model for future funding in the domestic industry.
A commentary angrily denies China's worsening pollution is a threat to the world environment and accuses developed countries of concocting the fallacy to monopolise global resources.
